pairs.why: A is a little chunkier and more toy-like, with fewer, bigger holes and a clear cover-over-comb build, which is closer to the real cards' simple shapes; B is almost the same but slightly more polished.
A's puffier, rounder cover and soft red caps match the soft volume of the real cards (scarf, fan) better than B's flatter, more literal metal plate.
A has chunkier proportions and soft, readable forms like the real cards, while B is a thinner, glossier plate that leans slightly toward a product render.
A is bigger and bolder, with rounded caps and a cushioned cover that fit the chunky toy look, while B is flatter and more mechanical.
A's chunky build, with rivets and a cover seam, reads like a real object in the game's soft style; B's thinner, slicker cover looks more generic.
A's softer, rounder cover and thick red caps match the plush volume of the real cards better than B's flat plate.
A's puffy, rounded silhouette and soft highlights fit the real cards' toy finish more closely than B's flatter, glossier steel plate.
Nearly identical; A's larger, rounder form with soft caps reads a touch more like the real cards than B's sharper, glossier cover.
